speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help me evaluate your condition, how long have these symptoms been present, and do they feel like the room is spinning or more like a loss of balance?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) is unlikely due to the sustained nature of your symptoms; the clinical picture of constant, low-grade vertigo with nausea and partial relief from antihistamines is more consistent with vestibular neuritis or a viral labyrinthitis. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes, I will need to see the results of your inner ear evaluation and imaging. REQUEST TEST: Audiometry; REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Impression
